operations.comment: ; 10-Yard Fight: readable current-classification copy. Physical identities include the 16-byte
; iNES header.
; CPU $8000..$FFFF maps permanently to effective PRG banks [0,1,2,3].
; All ROM bytes are classified; code entry contracts do not assert natural reachability.
; Shared zero-page state. Scratch aliases deliberately cover several routine-local contracts.
; Temporary previous random seed.
; Eight-bit recurrence seed.
; Shared scratch/input low byte; routines document their contract.
; Shared scratch/input high byte.
; Shared pointer/subtraction-result low byte.
; Shared pointer/subtraction-result high byte or sprite palette flags.
; Shared arithmetic result or OAM offset.
; Shared arithmetic result high byte.
; Decimal conversion high digit.
; Collision/probe origin longitudinal low byte.
; Collision/probe origin longitudinal high byte.
; Collision/probe origin lateral coordinate.
; Collision longitudinal difference low byte.
; Collision difference high byte; also shift register for steering probes.
; Pairwise contact class zero/one/two.
; Simulation tick; low bits schedule cadence and animation.
; High byte of simulation tick.
; Vblank counter; also seeded as title timeout.
; Vblank counter high byte.
; Presentation counter and foreground completion sentinel.
; Negative enables the match-clock decrement; zero stops it.
; Clock seconds, wrapping at 60.
; Clock minutes; negative underflow is clamped.
; First side score low byte.
; First side score high byte.
; Second side score low byte.
; Second side score high byte.
; Maximum score low byte.
; Maximum score high byte.
; Unsigned addend applied to the selected 16-bit score; cleared with scores.

; Twice selected skill plus half parity.
; Mode saved across the attract demonstration.
; Y position for sprite text.
; Selected field-map descriptor.
; Negative for attract/demo; zero for ordinary game.

; Sign chooses the alternate/two-player mode.
; Negative selects title/menu; overflow selects render-only presentation.
; Negative marks alternate saved-ball/side-change state.
; Bit six records pause toggle.
; Negative skips NMI work; cleared by common epilogue.
; Retained synthesized demo direction.
; Five logical scoreboard digits; followed by paired output rows.
; Five upper-row digit tiles.
; Five lower-row digit tiles.
; 16 or 32 palette bytes.
; Padded field scroll low byte.
; Padded field page plus direction bit seven.

; Ball lateral coordinate.

; Ball longitudinal world coordinate high byte.

; Aimed ball target longitudinal high byte.

; Packed play completion/result bits; $E8 ends live foreground wait.

; Next longitudinal field target high byte.
; Zero-based down counter.
; Packed/display distance to marker.
; Longitudinal down/first-down marker low byte.
; Longitudinal down/first-down marker high byte.
; Controlled-player contact/action counter.
; Enables special animation overlays.
; Zero bypasses saved-progress test; other values select comparison.
; Controlled-player cadence; reused as previous menu buttons.
; Stored kickoff longitudinal coordinate low byte.
; Stored kickoff longitudinal coordinate high byte.
; Countdown hiding temporary sprites.
; Saved ball/possession longitudinal low byte.
; Saved ball/possession longitudinal high byte.
; Scoring/end-event selector.
; Negative enables the alternate kick path.
; Eight bytes: two Y,tile,attribute,X sprite records.
; Selected player-record offset; $FF means none.
; Lateral maximum receiver record offset.
; Lateral minimum receiver record offset.
; Countdown triggering kickoff state release.
; Five formatted score tiles plus one terminator/work byte.
; 32-byte palette RAM shadow.
; Skill-dependent parameter pair low byte; consumer role unresolved.
; Skill-dependent parameter pair high byte.
; Four channel-class bytes.
; Four remaining note-duration counters.
; Four stream header/control bytes.
; Four stream positions: zero initializes, $FF inactive.
; Four stream pointer low bytes.
; Four stream pointer high bytes.
; Four loop counters.
; Four cached first APU register values.
; Channel number times four.
; APU status enable shadow.
; New active-side/controller or synthesized AI input.
; New opposing-side input; scratch during edge calculation.
; Controller one packed held bits: right $80, left $40, down $20, up $10, Start $08, Select $04, B $02, A $01.
; Controller two packed held bits, same layout.
; Previous low controller-one bits for edge calculation.
; PPUCTRL shadow.
; PPUMASK shadow.
; Presentation timeout decremented every 16 simulation ticks.
; PPUSCROLL first write.
; PPUSCROLL second write.
; Low five bits index the NMI handler pointer table.
; First skill-dependent timing byte.
; Second skill-dependent timing byte.
; Ball flight/action timer, also used as an expiry sentinel.
; Primary player record selected for probes.
; Eight-direction probe index.
; Inverted eight-probe collision mask.
; Preferred horizontal AI direction bits.
; Sign chooses which team/score/input/field orientation is active.
; Controller or AI direction/action byte consumed by player logic.
; Controlled-player motion selector.
; Player records: 18 slots, first team offsets $00..$40, opposing team $48..$88.
; Each eight-byte record holds state, packed direction, two state-local bytes, lateral X,
; longitudinal Y low/high and saved animation ID. State-local bytes change meaning by handler.
; VramRowQueue: address high, address low, 32 tile bytes.
; VramFiveTileQueue: eight records of address high, low, five tile bytes (stride seven).
; VramTwoTileQueue: twelve records of address high, low, two tile bytes (stride four).
; A negative first address high byte marks an empty queue.
; ContactMatrix: nine rows of sixteen bytes, first nine populated with contact classes.
; FieldMap: $8E strip descriptor bytes; TileRowScratch: 32 decompressed tiles.
; TileRowScratch shares CPU stack page $0100; ordinary stack activity uses its upper end.
; OamBuffer: 64 four-byte Y,tile,attributes,X sprite records, DMA page $07.
; TransientActor at $0390 has state,Y,X,timer,direction and saved world-Y/event bytes.
; ROM table addresses are equates so the frozen structural emission can remain intact.
; Skill strings selected in sixteen-byte steps; tile encoding, not ASCII.
; Two half labels eleven bytes apart.
; Five low/high parameter pairs indexed by even half/skill selector.
; Seconds/minutes pairs; demo and alternate mode have override entries.
; Skill-dependent timing bytes.
; Skill-dependent timing bytes selected by the clamped half/skill index.
; Five OAM-format records: Y,tile,attributes,X.
; Eleven little-endian handler addresses. State must stay within supported selectors; masking to five bits alone does not prove table extent.
; Eighteen four-byte state/X/Ylo/Yhi templates expanded to eight-byte player records.
; Three four-byte OAM records.
; Point values indexed by event selector; exact event names remain tentative.
; 32 NES palette indices.
; Six groups of three four-byte sprites; position bytes are relative to the transient actor.
; FF-terminated tile stream.
; Alternate FF-terminated possession tile stream.
; Thirteen tile IDs written after the side/half digit.
; Eight synthesized direction candidates.
; Eight-byte field attribute pattern repeated across nametables.
; Eight-byte alternate field attribute pattern.
; Eight-byte final attribute pattern.
; Sprite tile IDs; text writer indexes a caller-selected bounded subset.
; FF-terminated result heading.
; FF-terminated alternate-mode result heading.
; FF-terminated alternate result detail.
; Two palette-index pairs selected by field page.
; Packed pairs of two-tile column graphics selected by side and alignment.
; Two tile IDs per logical digit, with an alternate bank for half-tile scroll alignment.
; Three four-byte OAM templates.
; Three-byte field-map patches selected in four-byte steps.
; Two-byte skill palette pairs.
; Five side-specific field descriptors.
; Little-endian pointers to compressed 32-tile strips. Decoder interprets zero,value,count runs and nonzero literals.
; RAM field-strip descriptor template, $8E bytes.
; Five ordinary-side field descriptors.
; Sixteen little-endian state-handler addresses. All targets are classified under the player dispatcher contract; natural production of every state remains unresolved.
; Four phase offsets for rotating player sprite allocation.
; Per-player OAM offsets selected with the phase offset.
; Eighteen four-byte formation offsets/state records, copied to RAM before randomized patches.
; Eight-byte default player record expanded to all 18 slots.
; Sixteen animation IDs indexed by direction high nibble.
; Eight direction groups × sixteen phase entries controlling movement frequency.
; Packed per-sprite palette/attribute nibbles.
; Animation ID lookup by direction and contextual offset. Exact reachable selector set remains open.
; Four eight-byte two-sprite templates consumed by the special rendering helper.
; Four-byte records: coordinate base, two fixed bytes and signed-choice jitter magnitude.
; Formation choice mask bytes; random-range reduction selects a bounded entry.
; Alternate direction/phase movement cadence.
; Four-frame animation selectors indexed by animation group and tick phase.
; Eight bytes per animation: two Y,tile,attributes,X sprite records.
; Randomized formation bit masks.
; Packed steering map; relative ball/player grid selects one nibble.
; Packed steering map contributing direction high bits.
; Twelve base periods stored high byte first; octave is applied by right shifts.
; Sixteen duration values.
; One enable bit per channel.
; Complementary channel-enable masks.
; Audio stream pool: header followed by two-byte note/command records. Named selectors establish entry addresses, not independent stream length.
; Nine rows of 22 tile IDs.
; 21 tile IDs written to nametable $2305.
; 14 tile IDs written to nametable $2345.
; 32 palette entries copied to PaletteBuffer.
; Seven tile IDs per mode label write.
; 32 bytes of title nametable attributes.
; Eight four-byte records: signed lateral delta and signed 16-bit longitudinal delta, plus one unused/pad byte.
; Four action/direction fragments for special steering lookup results.
; 256 mask-indexed direction/action bytes; high nibble $F selects the secondary action lookup.

; Contact stream consumed by channel one.
; Newly resolved table and hardware contracts. Table aliases are CPU views, not file offsets.
; iNES header: 2 × 16 KiB PRG, 1 × 8 KiB CHR, mapper zero, horizontal mirroring; no trainer.
; Disable rendering and interrupts, wait for two vblanks, initialize stack/APU state, then run
; the title/attract/game cycle. Fixed NROM execution view: banks 0,1,2,3 throughout.
; Reset audio, scores and display state before the title screen. Preserve the selected mode
; while the attract demonstration runs.
; Stop the title/demo audio and clear demo mode; this entry is also reached by unwinding the
; title wait's return address.
; Initialize the selected skill/mode, palettes and half counter, then enter play setup. This
; is a long-lived control entry, not an isolated returning initializer.
; Load skill-dependent time/AI settings, field tiles and palette; choose the active side from
; mode and half parity.
; Clear per-play state, establish ball/field origin, build player records and begin the
; kickoff sequence. Sentinels use $FF; zero often means an inactive counter.
; Wait with NMI enabled until the primary audio stream finishes. NMI owns simulation while the
; foreground waits.
; Run random/proximity/steering preparation while NMI advances play; wait for the result byte,
; then stop NMI for transition work.
; Test the match clock at a dead-ball boundary. A completed half can unwind directly into
; half/game transition; an active half returns carry clear.
; Recompute the next field target and restart normal play setup after the kickoff path.
; Clear movement/possession state and rebuild down, field and marker bookkeeping before
; arranging the next formation.
; Select the punt/change-of-side presentation from result flags and down/field progress;
; otherwise retain the current possession.
; Wait for the NMI transition result, then rebuild the formation and receiver selection.
; Wait for the audio cue while continuing collision/steering work, then expose the live-ball
; state.
; Run proximity and steering updates until one of the $E8 end-of-play result bits is set.
; Increment the down counter, blank rendering, and check whether the half has expired before
; another play.
; Demo mode returns to its caller; a normal completed game builds the result presentation and
; returns to the title cycle.
; Set the alternate kick state, clear transient actors, and run its formation/selection/result
; loop. The exact distinction between kick types remains tentative.
; Await the primary cue before live kick processing.
; Continue steering/proximity work until a kick/end-of-play result appears; resume down or
; play setup from the clock/result state.
; Add 24 field units to the ball's longitudinal coordinate and return the 16-bit target in
; NextTargetLo/Hi.
; Select one of two half labels by parity and copy its FF-terminated tile string to nametable
; Clamp skill/half index for its text table, draw the skill name at $2B08, and draw the half
; label at $2B48.
; SkillTextTiles at CPU $8329: Skill strings selected in sixteen-byte steps; tile encoding,
; not ASCII.
; HalfTextTiles at CPU $8379: Two half labels eleven bytes apart.
; Clear the PPUMASK shadow and scroll-position pair. The caller controls when this shadow
; becomes hardware state.
; Clear the field and OAM, load a uniform palette and build the end-of-game scoreboard/message.
; Clamp the half/skill selector, then select clock, AI parameters and two player timing
; settings. Demo and two-player mode override some table indices.
; SkillParameterPairs at CPU $83EC: Five low/high parameter pairs indexed by even half/skill
; selector.
; InitialClockPairs at CPU $83F6: Seconds/minutes pairs; demo and alternate mode have override
; entries.
; SkillTimingTableA at CPU $840C: Skill-dependent timing bytes.
; SkillTimingTableB at CPU $8414: Skill-dependent timing bytes selected by the clamped
; half/skill index.
; Clear RAM page $0600, including saved per-player direction state.
; Reset scroll/base nametable state, update title or skill selection, and finish through the
; shared NMI epilogue.
; Update the timed presentation and continue into sprite/scroll rendering.
; Prepare scrolling, render player sprites, then continue through the shared NMI epilogue.
; Enter the common sprite update after a presentation handler.
; Prepare scroll buffers, process all 18 player slots unless this presentation suppresses
; them, and finish OAM/clock work.
; Save CPU registers, DMA OAM page $07, flush previous-frame VRAM work, read controllers,
; update AI/audio, and dispatch the current frame state. Main-thread handshakes prevent
; re-entry.
; Flush buffered display writes, advance the vblank counter, sample both controllers and
; update steering/audio before simulation dispatch.
; Advance simulation counters and clear the signed one-frame field delta; dispatch through the
; 11-entry NMI handler table using FrameState & $1F.
; Move the ball, dispatch each player record, update scroll/sprites and yardage markers, then
; tick the match clock.
; Complete ball marker and clock updates after an individual frame handler has drawn players.
; Check Start/pause before entering the common handshake-clearing epilogue.
; Clear the NMI handshake, restore Y, X and A, and return from NMI. The nested-NMI skip entry
; bypasses the handshake clear.
; IRQ vector targets the shared RTI at the end of the NMI epilogue; no separate IRQ service is
; established.
; React to a new Start press. Demo mode abandons the current stack and restarts the title;
; ordinary play toggles pause presentation and simulation flags.
; Hide the five pause sprites by moving their OAM Y bytes to $F0.
; Copy five four-byte sprite records into OAM at $0760.
; PauseSpriteRecords at CPU $8555: Five OAM-format records: Y,tile,attributes,X.
; NmiHandlerPointers at CPU $8569: Eleven little-endian handler addresses. State must stay
; within supported selectors; masking to five bits alone does not prove table extent.
; Resolve a delayed player-state change, then decrement seconds/minutes once per 16 simulation
; ticks while the clock-enable byte is negative. Clamp underflow to zero.
; Advance X by the eight-byte player stride, select team palette flags and render the saved
; animation. Caller bounds the 18-slot iteration.
; Clear 18 player records, load state/position templates, offset one team by skill, initialize
; ball/camera and copy kickoff sprites.
; KickoffPlayerTemplates at CPU $8691: Eighteen four-byte state/X/Ylo/Yhi templates expanded
; to eight-byte player records.
; KickoffSpriteRecords at CPU $86D9: Three four-byte OAM records.
; Advance the kickoff player's longitudinal position every fourth tick, switch frame state at
; the target, and draw all players with kickoff animations.
; Count down the kicking player's state timer, trigger kick audio/clock/selection at the
; release frame, and render the remaining players.
; Update the ball's special sprite and forward motion, then advance state when the stored
; kickoff position is crossed.
; Move toward the next field target; on arrival set the foreground result flag and return from
; NMI.
; Count down and move the temporary actor near $0390, render its three-sprite image, and set
; result bit $10 at expiry.
; Select among three ball sprite arrangements from distance to the kickoff point and current
; field position.
; Hide three temporary OAM sprites when their countdown expires.
; Add the selected point-table value to the active side's score outside demo mode, then update
; the high score. Team selection follows ActiveSide's sign.
; PointValues at CPU $88C1: Point values indexed by event selector; exact event names remain
; tentative.
; Copy 32 bytes from the gameplay palette template into the RAM palette buffer.
; GameplayPalette at CPU $88D3: 32 NES palette indices.
; Disable NMI and clear the title-selection flag after the attract timer expires.
; Enable NMI title mode, accept Start and mode selection, or time out into the attract demo.
; Start deliberately discards this call's return address before entering game initialization.
; Update the two title choice tiles according to the mode sign, restore rendering, and reset
; PPU scroll/address latches.
; Clamp the ball's lateral coordinate to the usable field interval $45..$94.
; Set the NMI-enable bit in the PPUCTRL shadow and hardware register.
; Clear NMI enable in the PPUCTRL shadow and hardware register before foreground display/state
; work.
; Set a temporary actor, run result-dependent timed frame states/audio, test scoring and field
; progress, and display a result sprite sequence before returning to play setup.
; Classified non-code by bounded pattern/reference review; precise schema and game role remain
; unresolved.
; Adjacent routines and available references were checked in round01 data review; no
; conflicting code evidence.
; Choose a three-sprite template, offset its coordinates by the temporary actor position, and
; copy it into OAM $07C4.
; ResultSpriteTemplates at CPU $8ACC: Six groups of three four-byte sprites; position bytes
; are relative to the transient actor.
; Set down zero and nominal distance 16; derive the field marker from NextTarget-104, clamping
; it to $00B8..$0398, and adjust displayed distance near the boundary.
; Reinitialize down/distance unless the saved possession position proves progress; otherwise
; convert progress to display digits.
; If the ball is far enough on screen, place an FF-terminated possession-related message and
; run a timed presentation.
; Draw the alternate possession message before the shared timed presentation; exact wording
; remains encoded as tile IDs.
; Run frame state five until the simulation counter wraps, then disable NMI.
; Flip the active-side bit, reflect lateral and longitudinal ball coordinates, normalize the
; tile-scroll position, redraw the field, and reset the target/camera.
; Restore the baseline screen Y in the near-field boundary region.
; Limit the next target to $03FC, the far playable field boundary.
; Copy seven four-byte OAM records, then put the packed number nibbles into two tile fields.
; A zero high nibble is omitted by reusing the low-nibble path. The alternate entry hides all seven records.
; Seven OAM records (Y, tile, attributes, X), copied backwards by DrawSevenSpriteNumber.
; Their X coordinates increase by eight; the display uses two patched tile fields.
; Subtract the field marker from the saved possession position and divide by eight. Return
; carry set for positive progress of at least one eight-unit step.
; Subtract caller-supplied distance from ball position, convert to padded scroll/nametable
; coordinates and return a nametable destination six tiles in.
; Set a negative destination sentinel through the shared ScratchHi store/return tail.
; The constant branch skips the following strings; their bytes are not executed.
; Four low-domain, $FF-terminated tile strings. Two have established pointers to the
; existing string writer; callers for the other two remain unresolved.
; Return carry set immediately for the zero sentinel; otherwise compare the saved progress
; against the field marker.
; Check the ordinary ball or alternate saved ball coordinate against $03E8. Outside demo,
; award two points to the other side and set result bit $02 and a side-change marker.
; Reset player positions, calculate a nametable destination near the ball and write a
; side/half digit followed by 13 message tiles.
; FieldResultTiles at CPU $8DD5: Thirteen tile IDs written after the side/half digit.
; Present the result, normalize the near-boundary ball position, and, for a scoring event with
; time left, discard the return address and start a new play after applying side change.
; Strobe and read both serial controllers into held-byte shadows; compute new presses against
; previous low-nibble state. Swap active/opposing input bytes for the opposite side. Demo mode
; synthesizes input periodically.
; DemoDirectionChoices at CPU $8EBC: Eight synthesized direction candidates.
; Disable rendering and fill tile/attribute space with blank tile $30 and zero attributes,
; then restore the mask shadow.
; Fill OAM page $0700 with $F0, placing all sprite Y coordinates outside the visible image.
; Upload 32 RAM palette bytes; entry UploadBackgroundPalette uploads 16. Rendering is
; temporarily disabled and PPU address/scroll latches are restored afterward.
; Upload the caller-selected 16-byte background palette, entering the shared palette writer.
; Restore PPUCTRL and both scroll values after reading PPUSTATUS to reset the address latch.
; PPUMASK is restored by the palette writer before this entry, not by this entry itself.
; Advance an eight-bit linear recurrence: seed = seed*5+17 modulo 256. Return the updated seed
; in A.
; Copy the successful 16-bit subtraction result back into the input/remainder pair; shared by
; decimal conversion.
; Convert the unsigned 16-bit input to packed decimal digits using repeated subtraction of
; 10000,1000,100,10. Output $14/$15 packed digit pairs and $16 ten-thousands; input becomes
; remainder.
; Shared decimal conversion tail: repeatedly subtract ten, accumulating packed tens and
; leaving units in the remainder.
; Outside attract mode, add PendingScoreAddend to the selected 16-bit score, then share
; UpdateHighScore. ScoreSelectionFlags bit zero selects the second score; carry propagates to its high byte.
; Compare both 16-bit score values and retain their maximum in the high-score pair; arithmetic
; is unsigned binary here.
; Clear both two-byte scores and the pending score addend; preserve the high score.
; Convert the input word to five tiles, suppress leading zeroes with blank tile $30, and
; optionally write them to PPUDATA when incoming carry is set. Processor flags are preserved
; around conversion.
; Upload repeated field attribute patterns to both nametables, then restore rendering and
; scroll state.
; Write eight copies of the eight-byte attribute pattern to the current PPUDATA destination.
; FieldAttributePattern at CPU $90E5: Eight-byte field attribute pattern repeated across
; nametables.
; FieldAttributeMiddle at CPU $90ED: Eight-byte alternate field attribute pattern.
; FieldAttributeEnd at CPU $90F5: Eight-byte final attribute pattern.
; Mark the row and two column update queues empty with a negative leading address byte.
; Divide the 16-bit value in ScratchLo/Hi by the word in WorkLo/Hi using shifted subtraction.
; Return quotient in ResultLo/Hi and remainder in ScratchLo/Hi; divisor must be nonzero.
; With rendering disabled, copy the FF-terminated tile stream at WorkLo/Hi to PPU address
; ScratchHi:ScratchLo. A negative destination high byte skips the copy; then restore PPU
; state.
; Carry clear means time remains. On expiry advance the half/stage counters and test
; scores/mode; an intermediate half discards its caller and restarts half setup after a result
; screen.
; Present an alternate-mode half screen. Bound the half index, write headings, scores
; and attributes to VRAM, then flash the seven-sprite caption during a finite timed wait.
; The suffix helper writes the selected score index followed by two fixed tiles.
; Set two fixed nametable destinations and write each five-tile score using the shared
; formatter.
; Supply the high score byte and request immediate PPUDATA output through FormatScoreDigits.
; Write three OAM X positions eight pixels apart, starting at caller's OAM offset Y.
; Enter the three-sprite Y writer; its returning helper also has a direct entry at
; PlaceThreeSpriteYsInner.
; Write one supplied Y position into three OAM records separated by four bytes.
; Choose left or right caption placement from half parity. Set seven glyphs at Y=$50
; and fall through to the established sprite-text writer.
; Render a caller-bounded run of text sprites at Y=SpriteTextY, with eight-pixel X spacing,
; attributes one and tile lookup indexed by X.
; SpriteTextTileLookup at CPU $9304: Sprite tile IDs; text writer indexes a caller-selected
; bounded subset.
; ResultHeadingTiles at CPU $9312: FF-terminated result heading.
; AlternateResultTiles at CPU $931C: FF-terminated alternate-mode result heading.
; AlternateResultDetailTiles at CPU $9339: FF-terminated alternate result detail.
; Draw result headings and mode-dependent messages, then animate score sprites and blink the
; winning side for a finite interval.
; Wait for a 32-tick cadence, place three sprites per score group, choose mode-specific tiles,
; and blink the winner until the animation counter expires.
; Copy the PPUMASK shadow into hardware without changing the shadow.
; Fill every fourth RAM palette entry with A (shared universal-background entries), then
; upload the background palette.
; Write A then Y to PPUADDR. Caller must ensure the PPU address latch is in its expected
; first-write state.
; On alternate simulation ticks, derive padded tile position from ball position minus $B0 and
; update scroll while in its valid field interval. Select a palette pair from the high scroll
; page.
; ScrollPalettePairs at CPU $94D8: Two palette-index pairs selected by field page.
; Skip the row update and finish restoring normal field rendering.
; Blank rendering, alternate between a 32-tile row queue and two compact column queues, and
; restore the selected nametable/scroll and normal field mask.
; Alternate between row decompression and column/scoreboard assembly so the NMI writer has
; bounded work next frame.
; Convert padded world coordinates to a nametable address, select a strip descriptor from the
; RAM field map, expand literal or zero/value/count runs to 32 tiles, and queue the row.
; Patch the side-dependent field descriptor, blank rendering, and build/upload 32 successive
; tile rows, skipping the padded gap between 240-line pages.
; Load fixed marker sprites, choose mode-specific tile, and update ball/down markers; hide the
; down marker during kickoff states.
; Build eight five-tile and twelve two-tile VRAM records, crossing nametable boundaries
; safely. Assemble side graphics, scores, clock and down/distance into those buffers.
; SideColumnTiles at CPU $9894: Packed pairs of two-tile column graphics selected by side and
; alignment.
; Convert five logical digits into paired tiles, choosing one of two tile banks from scroll
; alignment, then copy each tile row into the five-byte column records.
; DigitTilePairs at CPU $9937: Two tile IDs per logical digit, with an alternate bank for
